trust_decision.summary: When Editor.AllowSVGScript is off, util.SanitizeSVG decides which href/xlink:href data: URIs in a served SVG are safe; at the pinned commit it uses a denylist (text/html, image/svg+xml, application/xhtml+xml), so other scriptable MIME types such as text/xml pass; the fix switches to an allowlist of raster image types.

landing_point.why: The summary names getDynamicIcon; its handler injects the raw `content` query parameter into the SVG (kernel/api/icon.go:159-161, kernel/api/icon.go:579-584) and then calls util.SanitizeSVG at kernel/api/icon.go:168, which leads directly to the data: denylist in kernel/util/misc.go:289-293.

fix_sites.entry_point: GET /api/icon/getDynamicIcon (registered without CheckAuth, kernel/api/router.go:36) and GET /assets/*path via serveSVG (kernel/server/serve.go:601, kernel/server/serve.go:617-633)
fix_sites.module_kind: shared sanitizer utility (kernel/util), one function, one hunk

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The fix touches only SanitizeSVG in kernel/util/misc.go:289-293. Its second caller, serveSVG at kernel/server/serve.go:617-633, is fixed for free because it shares the function; it is not a separate fix site.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The /history/*path and /repo/diff/*path routes are admin-only viewers of snapshot or diff copies that serve files raw through http.ServeFile, so a solver can argue they are a different feature and never went through SanitizeSVG.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: SVG assets that embed raster images as data:image/png, jpeg, gif or webp in <image href> must keep rendering. Plain-text and CJK icon content in getDynamicIcon type 8 and its `.action{` template rendering must also keep working. An over-broad fix that strips every data: href or HTML-escapes everything breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: xlink:href attribute (parsed by x/net/html as namespace xlink, key href, and also matched by the literal keys 'xlink:href' and 'xlinkhref')
data: URIs of any MIME type, now allowlisted by prefix (png/jpeg/gif/webp)
mixed case and embedded tab/CR/LF in the value, normalised before the check (kernel/util/misc.go:263-269)

O7_producer.where: kernel/api/icon.go:537-584 (generateTypeEightSVG builds the SVG from the raw query parameter `content`)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /history/*path serves history snapshot files, including .svg assets, raw through http.ServeFile with no SanitizeSVG under AllowSVGScript=false
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Admin-only history viewer that serves stored snapshots, not live assets; it never went through serveSVG
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as serveSVG (kernel/server/serve.go), different function; 1 package from the fix site

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /repo/diff/*path serves repo-diff temp copies of files, including .svg, raw through http.ServeFile without SanitizeSVG
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Admin-only data-repo diff viewer serving temp files; a neighbouring feature to asset serving
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as serveSVG, different function

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Static file groups /emojis/, /widgets/, /plugins/, /templates/ and /public/ (the last without CheckAuth) serve .svg files with no SanitizeSVG
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: These directories hold user-installed trusted content that is also served as .html/.js, so SVG sanitising there would not close anything; this is a weak O8 candidate

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Make /history/*path call serveSVG for .svg, the same way /assets does, but through a copy of the sanitizer or a separate data: check that keeps the old denylist
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: /assets already special-cases SVG at kernel/server/serve.go:601; a maintainer adding the same handling to history preview could easily have copied the pre-fix denylist.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A style-attribute url(data:...) check next to the existing url(javascript:) check, written as a denylist
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The style branch already does denylist substring checks for javascript:/expression(; extending it to data: URIs by the same idiom is natural.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second dynamic-SVG endpoint, e.g. a sibling icon/badge generator, with its own inline data: filter instead of calling util.SanitizeSVG
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: icon.go builds SVG with fmt.Sprintf from query parameters; a parallel generator with its own filter would be a realistic second implementation.

O9_family: XSS via incomplete SVG sanitizer denylist (CWE-184 incomplete list of disallowed inputs, CWE-79)

O10_build.language: Go (kernel); TypeScript frontend not needed for this area
O10_build.toolchain: Go 1.25.4 (kernel/go.mod:3), golang.org/x/net v0.52.0 (kernel/go.mod:83); kernel build may need CGO and the sqlite fts5 tag (unverified)
O10_build.project_tests: No *_test.go in kernel/util at the pinned commit; SanitizeSVG has no unit tests. A hidden test can call util.SanitizeSVG directly, or call the getDynamicIcon handler through gin with httptest.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add "text/xml" (and maybe application/xml) to the existing data: denylist at kernel/util/misc.go:290 instead of switching to an allowlist.

out_of_scope_notes: getDynamicIcon is registered without CheckAuth (kernel/api/router.go:36) and inserts the raw `content` into the SVG body (kernel/api/icon.go:582); the endpoint's only defence is SanitizeSVG, so other bypasses of that sanitizer (e.g. a <style> element, or attributes other than href) would be separate issues.
When AllowSVGScript is on, sanitising is skipped entirely by design (kernel/conf/editor.go:22).
unverified: Whether /history and /repo/diff can actually hold attacker-influenced .svg content in practice (e.g. synced snapshot assets) was not traced.
Whether serveThumbnail (kernel/server/serve.go:635) can produce SVG output was not checked.
present_in_latest is unknown for every O8 route because no latest release was provided.
The CGO/fts5 build requirement for the kernel was not checked.
